Thought: I need to determine the characteristic cation of quaternary ammonium salts. Let me analyze each option.

Quaternary ammonium salts are compounds where all four hydrogen atoms of the ammonium cation (NH₄⁺) have been replaced by organic groups (R). The "quaternary" refers to the nitrogen atom being bonded to four organic groups, making it a positively charged species.

Let's examine each option:
A. [NH4]+ - This is the ammonium ion with no organic substituents, so it's not quaternary.
B. [NHR3]+ - This has one hydrogen and three organic groups (R), making it a tertiary ammonium ion.
C. [NR2]+ - This has two organic groups (R) and no hydrogens shown, which doesn't match the structure of an ammonium ion (which needs 4 bonds total).
D. [NR4]+ - This has four organic groups (R) attached to nitrogen, making it a quaternary ammonium ion.

The correct answer is D. [NR4]+, which represents a quaternary ammonium cation where all four positions around the nitrogen are occupied by organic groups.
